title: CAP resilience patterns
explain: External calls need resilience; pair retries with idempotency. (Tier 1–2 simulation fidelity — verify production details in official SAP docs.)
analogy: Think of "CAP resilience patterns" as a named building block you must explain under pressure.
whyItMatters: Without CAP resilience patterns, you mis-diagnose incidents and make weak architecture choices.
commonMistakes: Memorizing the name of CAP resilience patterns without a failure story
howToApply: Use CAP resilience patterns explicitly in a design defense sentence
mnemonic: NAME IT TO TAME IT: Say “CAP resilience patterns” + one failure mode out loud — if you can't, you don't own it yet. (CAP → mechanism → failure)
useCases: Discount approval near S/4 — choose placement using CAP resilience patterns without core mods.
Incident bridge: symptoms appear; use “CAP resilience patterns” to classify the failing hop before changing config.
Architecture review board: defend why you accepted residual risk around “CAP resilience patterns”.

designTradeoffs.whenChooseB: Tight transactional fidelity to S/4 BO
designTradeoffs.risk: Wrong placement creates dual-write or upgrade pain

designTradeoffs.whenChooseB: Internal-only tools with no external clients
designTradeoffs.risk: Wide APIs couple consumers to schema churn
Shared schemas block ownership and safe deploy
